messages:
maria: quick Q — trying to find raw request logs for request_id=abc12345. Console shows a span link for trace `1a2b3c` but when I follow the trace i only see spans, no raw nginx/ingress lines. anyone see this pattern?
ash: did you search the ingress pods directly? sometimes the LB rewrites headers and the request_id lands in the backend header (eg `x-backend-request-id`). quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=nginx-ingress` then `stern nginx-ingress -n prod --since 1h | rg abc12345` :thumbsup:
leo: also confirm the header name. we have a few agents that use `x-request-id`, `x-correlation-id`, or `x-backend-request-id`. console trace -> span metadata will sometimes show the original header name under attributes. search both `request_id` and `x-request-id`.
ash: example stern command that helped me yesterday:```stern -n prod 'nginx-ingress' --container nginx --since 2h | rg "abc12345|1a2b3c" -n``` if nothing shows, try the edge proxy (app=edge-proxy) and the LB (if you have client IP samples).
observability-bot: dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/1a2b3c (sample trace). Also note: trace sampling for the edge is 0.05 by default — if you have only one trace id it may not correlate to logs unless the request hit a sampled host.
maria: tried stern on nginx and edge-proxy, no hits. I do see the span in trace UI with `http.request.header.x-forwarded-for` set — but the `x-request-id` field is empty there. could LB be dropping it?
ash: yep, some GCLB configs drop custom headers to healthcheck/backends. check the LB rewrite rules and the ingress annotation `ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-set-headers` — if header is omitted the request id won't reach pods. Also check our envoy filter on edge-proxy that maps trace id -> x-request-id; sometimes it fails when the backend retries.
leo: alternate hunt: search logs by trace id fragment. in console try: `console search "trace_id:1a2b3c"` or `console search "span.trace.id:1a2b3c"` — console sometimes indexes trace ids under `span.trace.id`.
maria: good tip. one more thing — i noticed the app rewrites the id into `internal_req` header; grep for that too. searching all headers in stern output worked:```stern -n prod 'app=my-service' --since 30m | rg -i "abc12345|internal_req|x-backend-request-id"```
ash: if all else fails, pull the raw HTTP access logs from the LB (cloud console) for that minute — they include all headers before rewrite.
maria: sweet — that found it: LB had `x-backend-request-id: abc12345` and nginx had the id under `internal_req`. thanks! I'll update the service to mirror x-request-id -> internal_req to make future hunts easier. :raised_hands:
observability-bot: note added to ops runbook: "If no console raw lines for request_id, check LB raw logs and alternative header names (internal_req, x-backend-request-id, x-correlation-id)."
leo: +1. also file a small eval to include header mapping in our request-to-log playbook so new folks don't get stuck.
maria: will do a quick PR against docs later today and ping here when done. thanks all!
